change_ref: OpenSpec change local-ocr-backends (design D5, D6, D8, D9)
question: Does a local OCR backend that supports Arabic, Bengali and Devanagari read the 129 non-Latin pages well enough to keep many of them local, without making Latin pages worse, and does its confidence separate good pages from bad pages?
decision: Whether a follow-up change adds a second backend to the local OCR registry, and which one, with which confidence cut.

hypotheses.statement: At least one candidate arm (B Indra OCR, D Apple Vision) passes G1 to G4 for at least one script: median recall 0.70 or more on that script, at least 0.30 of that script's pages kept local by a leave-one-document-out cut with at most 0.05 of kept pages bad, Latin recall not worse than PP-OCRv6 Small beyond the stated margins, and 5.0 s per page or less on CPU. Apple Vision is not run on Bengali, so a pass for it can cover only Arabic and Devanagari.
hypotheses.null: No candidate arm passes G1 to G4 for any script.

hypotheses.statement: The page confidence of at least one arm ranks pages by recall: AUC 0.80 or more for the event recall at least 0.8, over the 229 pages.
At least one arm passes G1, G2 and G4 for a script and fails only G3 (Latin non-regression), so a script chooser would unlock it.

decision_rule: An arm is a candidate for script S when G1, G2, G3 and G4 all hold for S. PASS: at least one arm (B or D) is a candidate for at least one script; open a follow-up change that adds that backend with the cut this experiment picks. FAIL: no arm passes G1, G2 and G4 for any script; keep pp-ocrv6-small only. INCONCLUSIVE: an arm passes G1, G2 and G4 for a script and fails only G3; record that a script chooser would unlock it and adopt nothing now. The gate numbers are fixed before any run and do not move after it.
baseline: A PP-OCRv6 Small (stored Experiment 33 output, no rerun)
candidate: B Indra OCR 1.1.2; D Apple Vision through ocrmac 1.0.1

gates.value: median recall on the pages of script S
share of good pages (recall >= 0.8) kept local, scripts passing G1, leave-one-document-out cut
share of kept pages with recall < 0.5, same pages and cut
share of all pages of the scripts passing G1 that stay local
median over the 100 Latin pages of (arm recall minus PP-OCRv6 recall)
lowest stratum median of the same difference (print 30, old print 35, handwriting 35)
median over timed pages, warm-up excluded, one request at a time

gate_justification.G1: Experiment 37 reports dots.mocr medians of 0.985 (Devanagari), 0.887 (Bengali) and 0.873 (Arabic) against this reference. 0.70 is about 0.8 of the lowest, 0.873.
gate_justification.G2a: At 0.60, the cut sends at most 0.40 of the good pages to a 37.0 s engine (Experiment 37).
gate_justification.G2b: The Experiment 39 G2 bound: kept bad pages at most 0.05 of kept pages.
gate_justification.G2c: 0.30 of 129 pages is about 39 pages. 39 pages at 37.0 s is about 24 minutes saved per 129 pages against always. Below that the second backend does not pay for its dependency, licence and cut.
gate_justification.G3a: Small margin. Scans give no script verdict before OCR (Experiment 45), so a backend that reads every flagged page must not make Latin worse.
gate_justification.G3b: Wider margin because strata have 30 to 35 pages.
gate_justification.G4: The engine takes 37.0 s per page (Experiment 37). 5.0 s is about one seventh. PP-OCRv6 takes about 0.7 s per page (Experiment 45 (d)).

definitions.recall: Multiset token recall as in Experiment 33: build_labels.tokens and build_labels.recall, imported. Reference tokens are the split body text when it exists, else the first transcription (the rule of local_ocr._reference in Experiment 33 and score_recall.py in Experiment 37). A page with no output scores 0.
definitions.page_confidence: Mean of line confidences weighted by character count (change local-ocr-backends, design D5). Indra uses Line.conf; Apple Vision uses its line scores. Exploratory alternatives reported: minimum over lines of 10 or more characters; share of characters on lines at 0.8 or above.
definitions.cut_selection: Leave one document out over nine documents. For each held-out document, on the other eight documents choose the lowest cut on the grid 0.50, 0.55, ..., 0.95, 0.99 for which the pages at or above the cut have a share with recall below 0.5 of at most 0.05. No qualifying cut means the arm keeps no page in that fold. Apply the cut to the held-out document. Pool the nine results. The cut to register is the median of the nine chosen cuts, rounded to 0.05; it is reported and not gated.
definitions.timing: Wall-clock seconds per page, CPU, one request at a time, default thread settings of the runtime, first 3 pages of each arm not timed, model load time recorded once and apart. Arm D may use the Neural Engine and is reported as measured.

page_classes.non_latin: 129 pages: io01 48 (Devanagari), io02 16 and io03 5 (Arabic, 21 total), io07 60 (Bengali). The same set as Experiment 45.
page_classes.latin_sample: 100 pages drawn with seed 46 from pages that have a stored PP-OCRv6 row, a split reference transcription and at least one reference token. Strata: print io04 and io05, 30 pages; old print io06, 35 pages; handwriting rf06 and rf07, 35 pages.

arms.name: Indra OCR 1.1.2 (Datalab)
arms.licence: modified OpenRAIL-M; the operator reads the full licence before any run
arms.version: indra-ocr 1.1.2 (PyPI), onnxruntime 1.31.1, Python 3.12.15; weights datalab-to/indra-ocr tag v1.1.0, snapshot bd02167fdf2005a19962cc15188f8496a2c87d3b
arms.weights_sha256_method: SHA-256 of the sorted '<file sha>  <name>' lines of the 12 downloaded files (76.1 MB)

arms.name: Apple Vision through ocrmac 1.0.1
arms.bengali: not run on the 60 Bengali pages: no support. A pass for D can cover only Arabic and Devanagari.
arms.size: OS model; a few MB of Python packages
arms.version: ocrmac 1.0.1, pyobjc-framework-Vision 13.0, Python 3.12.15, macOS 27.2 (26B123), Apple M5 Pro, 64 GB

input_locations: Inputs are read only. Repository paths come first and the local data store second (<data store>/experiments/<experiment folder>/). Gitignored outputs live in the data store: the stored local OCR text, the page images, the reference transcriptions and the dots.mocr text. The runner reads the first copy it finds and checks its SHA-256 against this file.
preconditions: P1: the frozen hashes match. Stop on any difference.
P2: the non-Latin class equals the rows of the stored PP-OCRv6 file for io01, io02, io03 and io07 (129 pages, same keys).
P3: every Latin stratum has at least as many eligible pages as its draw (30, 35, 35). Stop and amend before any run if not.
P4: every page has a PNG in the Experiment 33 image folder, or the runner renders it with pypdfium2 and logs it.
P5: the Experiment 33 tokeniser imports and reproduces the stored body_recall of arm A on all 229 pages within 0.0005. Stop on any larger difference.
P6: before each arm, the operator has approved its downloads. Before arm B, the operator has read the Indra licence in full.
script_limit: Three Python files: run_arm.py (check, sample and one arm per call), summarise.py, analysis.py.

tolerance.metric: page recall, same arm, two runs

dropped_arms: RapidOCR and Tesseract were considered and dropped by the operator on 2026-11-04.

operator_decisions.retype_min_confidence: Deferred to the follow-up change that adds the first second backend.
operator_decisions.merge_seam_on_fail: No. On FAIL only the report merges and the code part is descoped.
operator_decisions.order: Experiment first; code groups only after PASS.
